spec_match.rationale: The spec forwards the abort reason to every body consumer; the matrix runs text/json/arrayBuffer/blob/bytes and a raw reader against real mid-flight aborts and reports identity per consumer — the full surface, not one representative call.

interactive.rationale: Reason-kind radios plus a run button drive six sequential real fetches; every cell is filled from the actual rejection object.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises a consumer-by-reason inspection table filled from real aborted fetches; that is precisely the behaviour.

edge_cases.rationale: bytes() absence is skipped honestly (observed on this Chromium 141), resolved-before-abort races are labelled inconclusive with a rerun hint, endpoint failures render per-row, and the no-argument mode explains why identity is n/a.

references.rationale: Links the fetch spec abort steps and both sibling concepts; the feature index carries the ChromeStatus link.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite covers the same contract for reader.read() and text() with identity checks that fail honestly pre-153; the matrix is the interactive superset across all six consumers.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP driver run 2026-08-16 after the final edit (f1-matrix.png): Error-reason run produced 5/5 ran consumers all 'no — substituted' with the two distinct pre-153 messages, bytes() skipped honestly; no-argument run showed every consumer with the minted AbortError; zero console errors; all net::ERR_ABORTED entries are the bannered intentional aborts.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts consumer-matrix-completed with ran/forwarded/substituted counts; rejection handlers attach before abort so no unhandled rejections reach telemetry.

design_system.rationale: Design-system variables throughout; identity cells pair emerald/amber left borders with explicit yes/no text on paper background.

accessibility.rationale: Semantic table with column and row headers, a keyboard-focusable scroll region (role=region + tabindex) for narrow screens, native radios/buttons, and a role=status summary line.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Feature harness passed both classes; the wide matrix scrolls inside its own overflow-x container so the 360px page body never scrolls horizontally.

openQuestions.title: Confirm bytes() row on a browser that implements Response.bytes()
openQuestions.detail: On this Chromium 141 the bytes() row reports 'not implemented' and is skipped honestly. On a newer engine the row should run like the others; verify the skippable branch does not mask a real rejection there.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel layout without horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Wide tabular content must scroll inside its own overflow-x:auto container; never let the page body scroll horizontally.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The matrix table has min-inline-size 640px inside a .table-wrap with overflow-x auto and keyboard focusability; the page body stays within the viewport at 360px.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible data table for probe results with row headers
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use th scope=col/row and convey status with text as well as colour.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Consumers are row headers, verdict cells carry explicit 'yes ✓ forwarded' / 'no — substituted' text alongside the coloured border.

summary: Inspection matrix across all six Response consumers filled from real sequential aborted fetches. On this pre-153 Chromium it demonstrates the inconsistent generic substitutions ('The user aborted a request.' vs 'BodyStreamBuffer was aborted') the spec text removes, and the no-argument mode verifies the minted AbortError default everywhere.
